findings.obs_text: In Psa 38:12 seek (H1245, H1875) stands seven and four words before meditate and names the ones who meditate treachery: those who seek the speaker's life and hurt.
In Psa 77:6 search (H2664) stands four words after meditate, in the clause that follows it: after meditating in his heart, the speaker's spirit searches.
findings.grounds: Then my spirit made a diligent search

findings.obs_text: In Act 10:19 looking for (G2212) stands eight words after pondering, in what the Spirit says while Peter ponders: men are seeking him.
findings.grounds: three men are looking for you

older.finding: the surface sense of seek departs from the neutral gloss in the idiom seek my life (Psa 38:12, 2Sa 4:8, Pro 29:10)
older.reason: it states a face of the seek words; the search collection owns it

older.finding: in Psa 38:12 the seeking is done by the hostile party and directed at the speaker's life and hurt
older.reason: it states the parties of the seeking in the verse; the search collection owns it

older.finding: in Psa 38:12 no other characteristic word stands beside the seeking (H1245); the other coded words are of other kinds
older.reason: it states what the data show of the words in Psa 38:12; six observations trace it, so it is kept and deferred to the search collection

older.finding: in Acts 10:19 the Spirit's speech announces the men's seeking; the two are related in the narrative
older.reason: it states how the seeking stands in the verse; the search collection owns it

older.finding: in Acts 10:19 the seeking is done by the three men and directed toward Peter
older.reason: it states the parties of the seeking; the search collection owns it

older.finding: the idiom seek the life or soul (Psa 38:12, 2Sa 4:8, Pro 29:10, Jer 4:30, Jer 11:21) means to seek to kill
older.reason: it states the sense of an idiom of the seek words; the search collection owns it
a process note on pre-filters and batches of an earlier reading; it states nothing of the verses and nothing of the inner being
it states how seeking works when it is illegitimate or restless; the search collection owns it

older.finding: search as a desire or purpose of the will directed to an object
older.reason: it states what the will does in searching; the search collection owns it

older.finding: seek as a hostile or purposed intent, the will set to harm another
older.reason: it states what the will does in hostile seeking; the search collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Jos 1:8 do (H6213A) stands five words after meditate, in the purpose of the meditation: to be careful to do all that is written.
findings.grounds: careful to do according to all that is written

findings.obs_text: In 1Ki 18:27 awakened (H3364, with H1931 at the same place) closes the verse, six words after musing, in the last of the states Elijah ascribes to the god: asleep and needing to be awakened. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through ponder; the verse pairs musing with waking instead.
In Psa 49:3 wisdom (H2451) and understanding (H8394) stand beside the meditation of the heart, in parallel: the mouth speaks wisdom and the heart's meditation is understanding.
findings.grounds: the meditation of my heart shall be understanding

findings.obs_text: In Psa 77:12 and Psa 143:5 ponder stands in parallel with meditate, in the next or the same line. The data places ponder in the wise collection, with the codes H1897 and H7878, the codes of the subgroup's own meditate.
findings.grounds: I ponder the work of your hands

findings.obs_text: In Psa 119:27 understand (H0995) opens the verse, three words before meditate: the speaker asks to understand the way of the precepts, and then he will meditate on God's works.
findings.grounds: Make me understand the way of your precepts
